correctness.rationale: A^2 is the span of the two part-sum vectors. The image of their zero product forces diagonal or anti-diagonal restriction to the characteristic square. In the diagonal case the Gram equations give invertible side blocks and force zero cross blocks, and the part-sum norms imply b=a^2 and a^3=1. The anti-diagonal case implies both part-size inequalities and therefore equality; an explicit side swap accounts for the second coset. Admissible dot-product hyperplanes are nondegenerate; they are orthogonal for odd characteristic and symplectic for characteristic two. Finite-field small cases were independently enumerated using the accompanying verification program. No finite check is presented as a substitute for the general proof.

value.rationale: An intrinsic natural problem is to identify all algebra automorphisms of an evolution algebra from a graph, rather than merely the graph-induced subgroup. The result classifies all automorphisms for an infinite two-parameter graph family over every admissible field, detects hidden nonmonomial symmetry, provides exact finite-field group orders, and explains the characteristic-two symplectic transition, with concrete K_{1,3} examples.
